title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its response to the 2020 Committee’s report on artificial intelligence and public standards, explaining how it plans to address the recommendations made. It highlights policy measures, commitments, and regulatory steps the government intends to take to ensure AI systems meet public expectations and uphold societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair, reliable and secure. The policy was issued after a request from several Secretary‑for‑State ministers to establish clear rules and safeguards for AI in the assessment sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report looks at how using copyrighted works in training AI systems can create legal challenges and opportunities, and it evaluates the potential risks and benefits. It also offers practical suggestions for developers and policymakers to handle copyright issues while advancing AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government responds to the House of Lords Select Committee's report on artificial intelligence, outlining its strategy to tackle the challenges highlighted in the “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” assessment. It commits to strengthening regulation, fostering innovation, and protecting citizens while ensuring the UK remains a global leader in safe, ethical AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document explains the purpose and scope of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence should fit into public standards. It also provides frequently asked questions to help members and stakeholders understand the committee’s duties, timelines, and decision‑making process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on governance of artificial intelligence. In its submission, the organization outlines its views on how AI should be regulated, including recommendations for policy frameworks and accountability mechanisms.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how AI will shape the regulation of medical products and outlines the steps for putting the AI White Paper principles into practice. It provides guidance to ensure that AI-driven medical devices and therapies remain safe, effective, and compliant with regulatory standards.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI-driven force for its size. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities to enhance operational readiness, decision‑making and strategic advantage while upholding high ethical and security standards.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness the benefits of AI while mitigating its risks. It focuses on improving transport services and safety through AI, while putting in place safeguards and regulations to address potential harms.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how copyright‑protected works are used to train and build AI systems. It outlines the legal framework under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, highlights progress made, and identifies challenges and recommendations for future compliance.
